Round 23 — the club logo in the 16px tab: framings and weights, priced, not applied

operator, 2026-11-25: "Regarding the logo, I feel like the gold color that is an established theme color of the website should be used in the logo a bit more prominently. Ensure some options you create to share with me consider that."

the third quarter of the Byrne logo item: put the ratified logo (row C, D483) in the tab. Operator framing of the ask: "square sphere-centred variant, full 240x150 letterbox, weight-scaled variants".

Nothing here is applied. Colour on this site is operator-ratified (D316) and the tab artifact is a one-way door for the site's own gates (D479), so this round prices and the pick stays the operator's. Every picture is the run's own raster: each row's SVG string, rasterized once at 8× the tab size by the same instrument that counted its pixels, then embedded. This page does not re-render anything, and a 16px picture here is 16 CSS px of a 128px raster — what a browser is actually asked to draw.

Everything below is a delta from this. public/favicon.svg is a 32×32 plate (viewBox "0 0 32 32", rx 6) painting #17130c and #faf6ec with the club's summand ∑ in serif 22 — 2 paints, which is why it passes. Its built copy dist/client/favicon.svg is identical (096094d983bfd5b2 / 096094d983bfd5b2), and the document parses: OK — the document rasterizes.

2. The drawing that has to fit (the logo's own numbers, not a re-drawing)

The plate is the hero's: 240×150u, ring 58u at (120,78), ink bounding box 117.4×117.46000000000001u at (61.3,19.240000000000002), sphere span 116u, strokes 1.3–1.4u, pole dot ⌀ 8u, right-angle arm 6u, feet 52u apart, equator dash 5/4. At 16px the tab is 16 device px, so the plate's 240u is 0.067 device px per unit and a 1.4u line is 0.09 device px — roughly 17× under the ~1.5 device px a line has to reach before it is ink at all (D119). That one sentence is why this round has weight rows.

Row T9 is the ratified hero colouring dropped into a tab: the gate refuses it on both grounds, because a tab logo is one ground and one glyph (rule 3) and two of row C's hues are reserved for join paths (rule 5). Rows G2–G4 are refused too — G2 for a third paint, G3/G4 because a solved gold literal is not a token @theme renders (rule 2). Row G1 passes with no new token and no ruling. The consequence for the ruling: a logo in the tab is not the hero's colouring at a smaller size. Something has to give — the tab gate's rules, the logo's colour table, or the logo's own colouring — and this round is priced so the operator chooses which, rather than discovering it after the pick (D479: a gate is re-derived, never bypassed).

4. Gold: the steer, the arithmetic, and what it does not settle

The operator's steer is quoted at the top of this page. There are two things on this site that "gold" could mean, and they cost opposite amounts.

The warm family (the site's own warm accent family, hue 35.7 — the family the role `gold` held before D316 renamed it) costs nothing: it is declared, shipped, and row G1 shows the gate accepting it. But note the asymmetry the matrix measures — --color-accent clears 4.5 on paper (5.77) and only 2.97 on ink, so which end of the warm family a ground may use is not a preference, it is which end clears the bar.

The true gold (a true gold/ochre hue, 62-75 — declared by NO token today (the role `gold` was retired with its name and the palette round refused the amber read, D316)) costs a new @theme token, which is the operator's act to take, so these rows are priced as declared CANDIDATES and are refused by check:favicon rule 2 as they stand.

  • The asymmetry, in one sentence. On paper the palest gold the 4.5 bar allows is L 55, which is below the lightness at which a hue 62–75 reads as gold — it reads bronze/ochre. On ink the darkest gold the bar allows is L 60, which does read as gold. So "gold on the light page" and "gold that looks like gold" are not simultaneously available, and the plate case inverts it: a gold GROUND is judged against the lines drawn over it at the pair bar, not at the 1.35 layer bar.
  • The same bytes appear twice. gold-line-ink and gold-plate-paper both solve to oklch(60.0% 0.14 75) → #b07100: one colour, two jobs.
  • What this round does NOT decide. Whether a hue 75 (39° from --color-accent) is admissible under round 3b's new-hue convention is not settled here — scripts/check-contrast.mjs runs its hue-gap rule over its own reserved map, and what that map reserves for the logo is a separate reading. Stated as a question with its numbers (26° at hue 62, 39° at hue 75), not as a refusal.

G3 sphere-centred, every line in a TRUE GOLD hue (~75) — the gold the palette does not declare

the honest price of a gold LINE, measured: on PAPER the solve lands at L 55 (`oklch(55% 0.14 75)` = `#a06200`, 4.59 against paper), which the record flags as BELOW the L 60 floor at which a hue ~75 colour reads as gold — a bronze line that satisfies the arithmetic and the eye separately. On INK it lands at L 60 (`#b07100`, 4.59 against ink) and that one reads as gold. So the same hue is a gold on the dark tab and a bronze on the light one, and the reason is the bar, not the hue. Either way the row costs a token @theme does not have: `check:favicon` refuses `#a06200` and `#b07100` with "is not a token (nearest: --color-accent renders #a2432a)", and the candidate names are printed as candidates, not as tokens. At 16px the row is also QUIETER than the ratified pair it replaces — T1 measures 87 any / 61 at3 px, this row 90 any / 62 at3 but a max contrast of 4.59 against 17.15 — so a gold line buys prominence in HUE and pays for it in CONTRAST.

framing: sphere — the ink bounding box of the whole figure — the sphere fills the tab · why this row exists: Byrne's yellow is the one ink row C could not use here (round 21 solved that window); this row asks the same question at tab size instead of hero size

G4 the full 240x150 plate, and the PLATE ITSELF is the gold

the gold with the most area — and the price that corrects a guess: a gold GROUND is not judged by the 1.35 layer bar, it is judged by the gate's 4.5 PAIR bar against the lines drawn over it, so the solve lands at L 60 under `ink` lines (`#b07100`, 4.59, reads as gold) and at L 55 under `paper` lines (`#a06200`, 4.59, BELOW the gold-ness floor). Gold on the light page, bronze on the dark one — the mirror image of the gold-line row, because the plate swaps which colour it is measured against. It is also the row that changes what the tab's ground MEANS: a gold plate is the site's colour replacing the browser's own background, and the 96 blank px a 240x150 plate leaves in a 16px slot (37.5% of the tab, measured) become gold bands. Costs a token @theme does not have.

framing: plate — the drawing exactly as the hero draws it, non-square · why this row exists: 1847 printing shows a diagram on a tinted plate: the colour is the surface the figure sits on, which is the one place a gold has room in this palette (the LAYER bar is 1.35, not 4.5)

6. How to read this page

  • Row N0 is the hero's drawing dropped into the tab with nothing tuned: at 16px it has 0 pixels at or over the 3.0 bar on paper and 0 on ink (its best contrast there is 2.09 / 2.80). Everything that follows exists because of that sentence.
  • T1–T4, T7–T9 centre the tab on the sphere and change only the stroke weight (and, in T7, the padding, and in T8/T9 the colour plan). T5/T6 put the whole 240×150 plate in the tab: T5 letterboxes it, so 96 of 256 tab px (37.5%) are the ground showing through with no logo on it.
  • Read three columns before liking a weight. The at/over 3.0 count is legibility. The survival table is which of the eight shapes still lands — at 16px some of them land on a single pixel. The dash table is whether the rear arc is still dashed: where it reads FUSED, the sphere has lost its only depth cue and reads as a circle with lines on it. The clip table is what the framing pushes outside its own frame and the tab therefore cannot show.
  • The two grounds are not decoration. A browser draws the tab on whatever chrome colour the user's browser and OS put behind it. Paper is the light chrome, ink the dark one; a colour that works on one can fail on the other and the artifact has to be a single file.
  • The pictures are the measurement. True size first, then the identical raster at 8×. No zoom, no re-render, no CSS filter: if a shape is gone at 16px it is gone in the browser too, and the firefox column above each row is the check on that (librsvg | firefox paired per size).
  • The delegate's ranked recommendation is not on this page. It belongs to the session report and .notes/NEXT.md, where it carries its pros, cons and the measurement that would change it; a specimen prices, it does not argue (D160).
  • Specimen chrome only: this page's own type and spacing are not the site's. The photographs are the run's raster.
